Cable Schedule Example With Sample Entries

Cable schedule example entries make the 10 columns easier to follow. The rows below show a typical set for one flow transmitter loop: a branch cable from the field instrument to a junction box, then a multipair main cable from the junction box to the marshalling cabinet. The tags, sizes and lengths are sample values for illustration only.

Cable no.TypeSize and coresFromToRouteLength (m)
IC FT1001Single pair, IS1 pair × 1.5 sq mm, overall screenFT1001 terminal 1, 2JB 101 terminal 1, 2Tray T145
IC TT1002Triad, IS1 triad × 1.5 sq mm, overall screenTT1002 terminal 1, 2, 3JB 101 terminal 3, 4, 5Tray T138
MC JB101Multipair, IS12 pair × 1.0 sq mm, individual and overall screen, armouredJB 101Marshalling cabinet MC 01Tray T1, trench TR2160

How to Read and Fill Each Row

  1. Give every cable a unique number that appears only once in the schedule.
  2. Match the cable type to the signal and keep IS and non IS cables in separate rows and routes.
  3. Enter both ends with the tag and terminal numbers so the site team can terminate without guessing.
  4. List the tray or trench sections in order, which later feeds the tray fill check.
  5. Add a length margin to the routed length and record spare pairs in the remarks column.

Remember that the schedule length is only an estimate. On site the cable is cut to the real routed length, so the final values are updated in the as built revision.
